expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: One of the better QB matchups of the week, and his WRs are healthy. Arizona ranks 30th in pass DVOA (+0.36 EPA per dropback allowed). The Rams defense looks slightly vulnerable, just enough that garbage-time Brissett could keep the Rams aggressive on offense.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Very much life Goff last week, Cardinals allow top 5 fantasy numbers to opposing QBs and continue to be a prime matchup. The Rams also have the highest implied on the slate, currently the only team above 30 points. Matthew Stafford is a cash staple this week.

players.notes: Team total at 51.5 points against a weak secondary allowing big numbers.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Any week ending in a number is a good week to target Josh Allen. He ran for 7 touchdowns in the first 4 games and followed that with 121 yards and a score against the Rams in Week 5. No quarterback has ever averaged more than 10.8 rushing fantasy points per game in a season, and Allen is at 14.8, so that pace will cool off. He still has room to grow as a passer and always has rushing upside. The Raiders are 29th in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks.

players.notes: Elite rushing floor facing a struggling Raiders defense ranked 29th.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Tyler Shough leads all quarterbacks in expected fantasy points per game at 23.7. The Saints play at the NFL’s fastest pace with an above-average pass rate over expectation, and their poor defense keeps the offense aggressive. The total looks mediocre, but this game has shootout potential if Jameis Winston plays well. The Giants are 23rd in EPA allowed per dropback and 25th in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Shough predictably had a down game in a brutal Vikings matchup after a sneaky good Falcons defense the week before. The Giants are a far better matchup, and the Saints cannot run the ball competently enough to not lean on Shough and the passing game.

players.notes: Leads all quarterbacks in expected fantasy points in a fast-paced offense.
Strong passing volume projection as a solid home favorite.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Great price on DraftKings. Buffalo ranks 28th in pass DVOA and is soft in its coverages. The Bills defense continues to give up large chunks of points, with the Chargers game being the only one where they played decently, and we now know what the Chargers are on offense.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Relatively cheap price on both sites and faces a Buffalo defense that has allowed the 3rd most DK pts and 4th most FD pts to opposing QBs. The Bills also rank bottom 5 in pass DVOA and could be down some key defensive pieces. Raiders are tied for the 5th highest implied team total at the moment and the ownership doesn't seem to reflect that. Love Kirko Chainz in GPPs.

players.notes: High game total environment with a 53.5-point over under against Buffalo.
High game total of 52.5 points in a potential shootout against Chicago.
Heavy home favorite with a solid implied team total of 41.5 points.
Solid volume projection as a 7-point home favorite against Tennessee.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: I am always going to have interest in a 4K QB on DK, especially against a poor Panthers defense. I think McKee is on the better end of backup QBs, and he gets DeVonta Smith back from injury.

players.notes: Value option at minimum price facing a weak Panthers defense with Smith back.
Massive volume workhorse with elite goal-line role in a high game total.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Bijan Robinson leads the NFL in rushing yards (580) and touches per game (24). He has run a route on 52% of dropbacks, seen 88% of the team’s carries inside the 5, and is 2nd in the NFL in rushing yards over expectation. The Bears are 27th in EPA against the run and will be without starting defensive ends Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo, so the matchup is even better than it looks. This is a tremendous week to spend up at running back.

players.notes: Leads the NFL in touches facing a depleted run defense missing key starters.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: True cowbell RB with over 80% of the backfield touches (95% of the redzone rushes). Chiefs are big home favorite vs the Chargers, who already face the 4th most rushing attempts per game. Walker leads the league in rushing over expected and forced missed tackles. Safe in all formats and is simming extremely well.

players.notes: Heavy home favorite with strong projected workload and ceiling.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: New Orleans ranks 32nd in rush DVOA and has allowed the most RB rushing fantasy points in the league (25.3 per game). This goes one of two ways: They either feed him and let him shake off the stink of that game-costing fumble, or they cut back his workload. I tend to think they feed him.

players.notes: Value running back in a close matchup with a 46.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: 510 yards and nine total touchdowns in just the last two meetings against Tennessee for Taylor. If you believe in RvD (runner vs. defense), then this jumps out. Taylor is still good, Indy can still run the ball, and Tennessee is still bad on defense.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Jonathan Taylor doesn’t project as well as some of the other expensive running backs, but he’s my favorite by far, especially if ownership stays middling. He’s averaging 20 fantasy points per game even though the Colts are bottom 10 in EPA on both offense and defense. This week he should finally get a favorable game script as a 7-point home favorite against the Titans. He has played 82% of snaps, run a route on 58% of dropbacks, and seen 79% of the team’s carries inside the 5. This feels like a multi-touchdown week for #28.

players.notes: Favorable game script as a 7-point home favorite with heavy red-zone usage.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Hubbard has the exact same role as Rhamondre Stevenson does but comes at a massively discounted ownership this weekend.

players.notes: Value option in a tight matchup against Arizona.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Cook is in for one of his eruptions against this Raiders defense. They've allowed the 2nd most run plays of 10+ yards, and we've yet to see James Cook with a run longer than 35 yards. The big ones are coming, and he's going to have the opportunity to do so here with the Bills leading the league in yards before contact per attempt and the Raiders defense last in the league in yards before contact.

players.notes: Poised for explosive runs against a defense allowing high yards before contact.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Since the start of 2025, Henry averages more than 24 carries and 23 fantasy points in games with Tyler Huntley at quarterback. In all other games, he averages approximately 17 carries and 16 fantasy points. This is the perfect spot for the Ravens to lean on Henry, as road favorites.

players.notes: Heavy road favorite with a major boost in volume with Huntley at quarterback.
Solid tournament option with strong projected volume in a close game.
Tournament value option in a tight matchup against Carolina.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Puka has the best role of any wide receiver in the NFL against a bottom third defense in an absolute must win spot for his team.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Puka Nacua scored 31 fantasy points against the Eagles in Week 4 and 41 last week against the Bills. This game could be just as good for the Rams, who have a slate-high team total of 32.5. The Cardinals are 31st in EPA allowed per dropback and 27th in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to wide receivers. My only hesitation is the 12.5-point spread, but if Arizona keeps it competitive, this is an eruption spot for Nacua and the whole offense.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Feels like a must have in cash games this week. Faces a Cardinals team that has struggled to slow down opposing WRs, allowing 9.9 yards per target and league high 12.7% TD rate. Cardinals might also be without both their starting safeties.  Cardinals rank 31st in EPA/pass. Do not be afraid to play Puka in all formats, with or without Stafford.

players.notes: Elite role in a high-total game against a bottom-third pass defense.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Rashee Rice is on the wrong side of questionable with a hamstring injury, and Tyquan Thornton will likely miss the rest of the season. For at least one game, Xavier Worthy should be the Chiefs’ WR1. He has a 17% target share and a 24% air yards share through four games. The Chargers have seemingly given up on their season, so I’m not worried about the middling matchup on paper. Worthy isn’t priced for his expected role, and this slate badly needs value.

players.notes: Expanded role as the clear top target with injuries sidelining teammates.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Keep an eye on Penix, but it sounds like he's playing. If so, London draws favorable cornerback matchups, and Chicago has been one of the worst defenses against deep passes. With Penix's deep-ball accuracy, the Atlanta passing game has plenty of upside.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: As long as Michael Penix is his QB, London is an elite tier WR play, but he's not priced quite like it. With Penix at the helm, London has a 35% target share and 50% air yards share. He's effectively been similar to JSN/Puka types, but he's yet to find the end zone this year so far. That seems likely to change against a porous Bears defense that was just shredded by the Packers passing game.

players.notes: Massive target share and air yards share against a porous secondary.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Burden has a massively discounted price on Fanduel and is still reasonably priced on DK at 5.4k. I am a believer in the talent, the QB and the playcaller in what is a great matchup spot.

players.notes: Priced favorably on a fast-paced offense in a great matchup spot.
Strong target projection in a competitive matchup against New Orleans.
High-ceiling receiver in a fast-paced game environment against the Giants.
Strong upside in tournaments with a solid projected target volume.
Deep threat option in a game with a high 51.5-point total.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Isiah Likely has a top 5 role for any tight end in fantasy football with a healthy aDOT, second on the Giants in target share and first on his team in endzone targets. He is a core play for me against the Saints.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Likely leads all tight ends with a 30% target share and is coming off 11-of-13 targets for 93 yards and 2 touchdowns. The Giants are at home against the Saints, who are 1st in pace of play and 22nd in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to tight ends.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: If you aren't spending up for Bowers, Likely is the other must have in all formats (especially cash games). Likely leads all TEs this season with team target rate at 29.4%. He has been targeted on a little over 30% of his routes, which is only behind Bowers. Likely plays approximately 70% from the slot and 18% out wide where the Saints have been torched, allowing TEs from those alignments to account for 18-174-1 (on 20 targets) on the season.

players.notes: Elite tight end role leading his team in target share and red-zone looks.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: The Bills haven't been able to stop a team's primary weapon in the passing game at all this season. Amon-Ra St. Brown 9-142-2, Puka Nacua 17-138-1, Nico Collins 7-75-1, and now Bowers gets his turn to dominate in this matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: While the Bills defense is tough on tight ends, it is the 4th-best matchup for slot receivers in terms of schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game allowed. Bowers lined up 55.6% of the time as a slot receiver in Week 5 and just 18.5% inline.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Bowers is in a tier of his own at the TE position this season, being targeted on 30% of his routes with a league leading 2.92 YPRR among all TEs. He is only 4 yards behind Sam LaPorta for the lead in receiving yards among TEs, despite missing the first two games. He's also functionally a superstar WR who we get to play at TE, as he's lined up inline just 16% of the time. The Bills defense grades out as Cowboys and Lions level bad for me this season.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Bowers is essentially a WR1 who isn’t priced like one, averaging 24 fantasy points per game, which is 2nd only to Puka Nacua among slate pass catchers. The Raiders will likely be trailing against a Bills defense that might be bottom-five, so he should get peppered with targets. My favorite stack is Josh Allen solo with Bowers on the other side.

players.notes: Slot receiver usage against a struggling defense allowing massive tight end.
Reliable target volume in a game with a home-favorite script.
High-ceiling pass catcher in a high-total matchup against Los Angeles.
Budget tight end option with steady routes in a close divisional game.
Seam stretcher in a high-total game environment against Las Vegas.
Tournament tight end option with a favorable price and solid route.
Red-zone weapon in a fast-paced matchup against the Giants.
